title: Platform systems & services — dashboards, alerts, runbooks, roadmap, and team wiki (Q1 2026 retrospective)
author: Jordan Lee
body:
Overview:

This page consolidates the eng-platform systems & services inventory, standards for dashboards and alerts, canonical runbooks for the top incident classes we saw in Q1 2026, a short retrospective with action items, and the roadmap for the next two quarters. Intended audience: platform engineers, SREs, and on-call responders.

Table of contents:
1. Systems & services inventory
2. Dashboards and alerts standards
3. Platform how-tos and templates
4. Runbooks (high-priority incident types)
5. Q1 2026 retrospective (incidents, root causes, actions)
6. Roadmap and near-term initiatives
7. Team wiki & ownership

---

1) Systems & services inventory

Short intro: This inventory covers the primary platform services that support Redwood’s inference runtime, orchestration, control plane, and developer-facing API. Each service entry lists owner, SLOs, critical dashboards, and primary alerts.

- runtime-router-service
  - owner: eng-serving-runtime (owner: Miguel Alvarez)
  - primary SLOs: availability 99.95% monthly, p95 API latency < 120ms for small-text requests
  - critical dashboards: Runtime - Throughput & Latency, KV cache hit rate, Batch size distribution
  - primary alerts: routed_errors > 0.5% over 5m, p95_latency > 200ms for 5m, batch_backpressure_events > 10/min

- model-cache-service
  - owner: eng-platform (owner: Aisha Khan)
  - primary SLOs: cache hit-rate >= 85% for common prefixes, availability 99.9%
  - critical dashboards: Cache hit/miss by model & shard, memory pressure, eviction rates
  - primary alerts: cache_hit_rate < 70% for 10m, eviction_rate spike > 100/min

- control-plane-api
  - owner: eng-platform (owner: Priya Shah)
  - primary SLOs: API success rate >= 99.9% for control-plane endpoints, p99 < 1s for CRUD operations
  - critical dashboards: Control plane error budget burn, request rate by endpoint, DB replication lag
  - primary alerts: auth_fail_rate > 1% for 5m, db_replication_lag > 30s, error_budget_burn_rate > 5%/hr

- metrics-pipeline (Prometheus + Cortex + Loki + Grafana)
  - owner: eng-sre (owner: Jordan Lee)
  - primary SLOs: metrics ingestion latency < 30s, alert delivery to PagerDuty < 60s
  - critical dashboards: Ingestion lag, write throughput, TSDB compaction backlog
  - primary alerts: ingestion_lag > 60s, TSDB_compaction_errors > 0 for 5m

- tenant-auth-proxy
  - owner: eng-private-deployments (owner: Sara Ng)
  - primary SLOs: auth success rate >= 99.95% for tenant requests
  - critical dashboards: Auth latency, token KMS errors, regional error distribution
  - primary alerts: kms_decrypt_errors > 1/min, auth_5xx_rate > 0.2% for 5m

---

2) Dashboards and alerts standards

Purpose: Ensure observability consistency across services so on-call responders can act quickly and reduce cognitive load during incidents.

Dashboard standards (must-haves):
- One high-level service overview (SLO / error budget / critical KPIs) per service
- One performance dashboard (latencies, p50/p95/p99, QPS, concurrency)
- One resource dashboard (CPU/GPU utilization, memory, disk, network)
- One dependency dashboard (upstream services, DB lag, external API health)
- Color conventions: green (OK), yellow (warning approaching SLO), red (SLO violation)
- Template location: confluence link: /display/eng-platform/dashboard-templates and Grafana folders under org 'redwood-platform'

Alerting standards (policy):
- Alert types: Severity P0 (pager), P1 (pager + slack), P2 (slack), P3 (ticket)
- Default escalation: P0 -> immediate pager to on-call rotation -> if not acknowledged in 5m, page escalation contact -> on-call lead -> engineering manager
- Alert contents must include: problem statement, likely cause, affected scope, first-run diagnostic commands, runbook link, owner/team tag

Suggested thresholds (examples — tailor per service):
- Error rate alert: total_5xx_rate > 1% sustained for 5m -> P1
- Latency alert: p95_latency > 200ms for runtime-router-service for 5m -> P1; p99_latency > 500ms -> P0
- Resource pressure: GPU_utilization > 95% for 10m -> P1; GPU_out_of_memory events > 1/min -> P0
- Dependency: DB_replication_lag > 30s for 5m -> P1

Alert template (copy into Grafana/Alertmanager):
- summary: "{{service}} high error rate: {{expr}}"
- description: "Service {{service}} is experiencing an elevated error rate ({{value}}). Impact: {{impact}}. Runbook: {{runbook_link}}. On-call: {{oncall}}"

---

3) Platform how-tos and templates

This section contains short how-tos for common platform tasks and links to templates. Use these as canonical patterns when adding new services.

a) Create a new service dashboard (5 min checklist):
1. Fork dashboard template: /grafana/templates/service-overview.json
2. Replace variables for service name, SLO targets, Prometheus labels
3. Add panels: SLO, request rate, p50/p95/p99, error rate, resource usage, dependency health
4. Save under folder: redwood-platform/<service-name> and share view with eng-platform
5. Add dashboard link and owner to service Confluence page

b) Add a new alert (Alertmanager/Grafana):
1. Validate metric expression in Prometheus console
2. Use alert template and set severity label
3. Include runbook link and /api/oncall tag
4. Test by firing a synthetic alert (use test_alert helper)
5. Push change via CI: repo observability/alerts, open PR with runbook and reviewers

c) Onboarding a new platform engineer (first-week checklist):
- Access: join Slack channels #eng-platform, #oncall, #observability; get PagerDuty & Okta access
- Local dev: checkout infra repos, run local stack (make dev-stack up), verify metrics pipeline is accessible
- Training: pair with on-call buddy for 2 shifts, review runbooks for runtime-router-service and metrics-pipeline
- Docs: read dashboard templates and alerting standards

---

4) Runbooks (high-priority incident types)

Below are truncated, actionable runbooks for the most common incidents encountered in Q1. Each runbook starts with a short detection rule and a step-by-step mitigation procedure. Full runbooks live in the runbooks directory and should be linked from alerts.

Runbook A: Runtime routing degradation (high p95 latency or error rate)
- Detection: routed_errors > 0.5% for 5m OR p95_latency > 200ms for 5m
- Immediate actions (0-10min):
  1. Acknowledge pager and set incident channel (#inc-runtime-<time>)
  2. Check Runtime - Throughput & Latency dashboard (Grafana) for spikes in batch size, KV cache miss rate, or backend GPU errors
  3. Run diagnostics: curl control-plane/health; kubectl get pods -n runtime -o wide; promql: sum(rate(runtime_errors[5m])) by (reason)
  4. If GPU OOMs or node failures: scale down batch size via feature flag and divert new traffic to fallback model-variant using smart-routing policy (console -> routing -> fallback)
  5. If KV cache miss spike: warm caches by replaying recent prefixes from cache-replay job (job: cache-warmup/manual)
- Triage (10-60min):
  1. Capture request traces in Tempo for p95 requests and inspect KV cache behavior and kernel time
  2. If a deployment is implicated, roll back to last known good revision (k8s rollback: kubectl rollout undo deployment/runtime-router --to-revision=<rev>)
  3. Notify product and customers if SLOs are breached for >30m
- Post-incident: open postmortem and assign action items

Runbook B: Metrics ingestion lag / alert flapping
- Detection: metrics_ingestion_lag > 60s OR frequent alert-manager resend events
- Immediate actions:
  1. Acknowledge alert and check Prometheus remote_write throughput and Cortex ingest TPS
  2. Check retention indexes in TSDB and compaction backlog (Grafana: TSDB / compaction panel)
  3. If writer backlog > threshold: scale ingestion instances (k8s hpa patch deployment/metrics-ingest --replicas=+2) and open a ticket to eng-infra for persistent storage issues
  4. Silence noisy alerts while root cause is investigated (use /alertmanager/#silence and annotate incident)
- Triage: investigate partitioned write paths and network egress errors to object storage

Runbook C: Control-plane DB replication lag
- Detection: db_replication_lag > 30s for 5m
- Immediate actions:
  1. Check primary DB write latency and replication process (pg_stat_replication)
  2. If replication stalled, restart replica process and monitor WAL shipping queue size
  3. If I/O bound, request eng-infra to investigate underlying disk or network perf; engage DBA on-call

---

5) Q1 2026 retrospective (summary of incidents and action items)

Summary: Q1 saw three major incidents affecting customer-facing latency and observability reliability:
- Incident 2026-01-18: Runtime routing latency spike (root cause: inadvertent batch size increase in canary deployment). Impact: partial SLO breach for 45m.
  - Action items: add deployment-timeguard tests to CI to validate batch-size change (owner: eng-serving-runtime, due: 2026-03-15), default feature flags to safe minimum
- Incident 2026-02-09: Metrics ingestion disruption (root cause: TSDB compaction backlog after retention change). Impact: missing metrics for 2 hours and delayed alerts.
  - Action items: add capacity planning automation for metrics pipeline (owner: eng-sre, due: 2026-04-01), create runbook for retention changes
- Incident 2026-02-26: Control-plane DB replica lag after maintenance window (root cause: WAL shipping misconfiguration). Impact: control-plane API errors for internal tooling for 30m.
  - Action items: improve maintenance playbook and pre-checks; add replication-lag synthetic checks (owner: eng-platform, due: 2026-03-20)

Retrospective themes:
- Safe defaults: several issues caused by unvalidated config changes. We will add guardrails at commit/CI time to prevent risky config diffs from landing without test coverage or runbook updates.
- Observability coverage: add more dependency-level tracing and synthetic checks for critical datapaths (cache warm, ingestion path, DB replication).
- Runbook completeness: update runbooks to include exact prometheus queries, example kubectl commands, and postmortem templates.

---

6) Roadmap and near-term initiatives (Q2-Q3 2026)

Priority initiatives:
- Q2 2026 (owner: eng-platform / eng-sre)
  - Deployment timeguard CI checks for runtime configuration (batching, quant profiles) — due 2026-04-15
  - Metrics pipeline autoscaling & capacity planner — MVP due 2026-06-01
  - Dashboard template migration to new Grafana folders and dashboard tagging — due 2026-05-10

- Q3 2026 (owner: eng-serving-runtime / eng-platform)
  - Smart routing observability: per-route tracing and SLOs exposed in console — target 2026-08-01
  - Alert fatigue project: dedupe rules and suppression windows to reduce noisy alerts by 40% — target 2026-09-01

Longer-term (end of 2026):
- Platform observability unified view: combine metrics, logs, traces, and cost per token in a single SRE console tile
- Private deployment instrumentation (VPC/on-prem) Hardened observability agents and offline-forwarding for restricted networks

Roadmap notes: Each roadmap item must have an RFC and a milestone plan in product-docs/requirements before work starts.

7) Team wiki & ownership

Where to find more:
- Dashboard templates: /grafana/templates and confluence link: /display/eng-platform/dashboard-templates
- Runbooks directory: confluence link: /display/eng-platform/runbooks
- Oncall rotations & PagerDuty schedules: confluence link: /display/eng-platform/oncall

Service ownership (summary):
- eng-serving-runtime: runtime-router-service, benchmarking and perf suite (owner: Miguel Alvarez)
- eng-platform: model-cache-service, control-plane-api, tenancy tools (owner: Aisha Khan / Priya Shah)
- eng-sre: metrics-pipeline, alerts infrastructure (owner: Jordan Lee)
- eng-private-deployments: tenant-auth-proxy, packaging (owner: Sara Ng)

Next steps for team:
1. Owners to file RFCs for Q2 roadmap items within 2 weeks of this doc (by 2026-03-16)
2. Update runbooks for the three incidents listed and add PromQL snippets and k8s commands (owner: on-call teams, due 2026-03-30)
3. Schedule a game-day focused on metrics pipeline scaling (owner: eng-sre, target: 2026-04-08)

Appendix (quick links and diagnostic commands):
- Prometheus console: https://prometheus.redwood.internal/graph
- Grafana org: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/redwood-platform
- Trace search (Tempo): https://tempo.redwood.internal/search
- Common diagnostics:
  - kubectl top pods -n runtime
  - kubectl logs deployment/runtime-router -c runtime --since=10m | head -n 200
  - promql: sum(rate(runtime_errors[5m])) by (reason)

If you find missing items in this inventory or gaps in dashboards/runbooks, please open a PR against this page and ping the eng-platform channel.
